title: Macclesfield’s stadium set on fire in ‘suspected arson attempt’, club says
content:
An investigation has been opened after sixth-tier side Macclesfield’s stadium was set on fire.

Moss Rose was host to the National League club’s FA Cup win over holders Crystal Palace in January, one of the biggest upsets in the competition’s history.

Macclesfield released a statement in the early hours of Tuesday, saying a “suspected arson attempt” had occurred overnight.

Cheshire Police also confirmed via a statement to The Athletic that they were informed of a “deliberate fire” in two portable toilets at 1:15am and “enquiries are continuing into the circumstances”.

“Emergency services have responded immediately and are on site tackling the blaze in the affected area/s,” Macclesfield’s statement read.

“Despite understandable concern, we urge everyone to please avoid the area, anyone nearby to keep windows shut, and not to approach the stadium or disrupt the progress of the emergency services.

“We would like to reassure everyone that the situation is under control, there are no casualties and investigations are already underway into the cause of the fire.

“We would like to thank everyone for their concern and the timely response of those who alerted emergency services so quickly.”

Macclesfield last played at their home ground in a 4-1 loss to Fylde on February 24 and are next due to play there on Saturday as they host Chorley.

Following their victory over Palace in the FA Cup third round, they were knocked out by Brentford the round after. The suspected arson has come only a week after drama in the league saw King’s Lynn Town accused of deliberately flooding their home pitch before they were due to take on high-flying South Shields.

Macclesfield sit ninth in the National League North table ahead of their away match on Monday at Darlington.

The stadium lies around 17 miles from Manchester city centre in the north west of England.
